intro: If you've been wrestling with a cramped, dated bathroom in your Stoneley home and dreaming of something more practical and stylish, a wet room is well worth serious consideration. Wet rooms have become one of the most popular bathroom upgrades across Lancashire, and it's easy to see why — they're easier to clean, accessible for all ages, and they add genuine value to a property. Whether you're looking to modernise a period cottage in the older parts of Stoneley or upgrade a family bathroom in a newer estate, a properly installed wet room transforms daily life. Done right, it's a long-term investment rather than just a cosmetic change.
localContext: Stoneley's housing stock throws up some interesting challenges when it comes to wet room installation. The older stone-built properties and period cottages that characterise much of the town often have solid floors, uneven subfloors, or original timber joists that need careful assessment before any waterproofing can begin. Getting the falls and drainage right in a room that wasn't designed with wet room principles in mind takes real skill and experience — corners cut here lead to damp problems that are expensive to fix later. Modern estates in Stoneley present a different set of considerations, typically offering more straightforward subfloor conditions but sometimes limited space for tanking and drainage positioning. It's also worth noting that Stoneley sits in a moderately hard water area, which means limescale build-up on screens, fittings, and shower heads is a genuine day-to-day concern. Choosing the right fittings and factoring in a water softener or descaling system during the installation can save a lot of maintenance headaches further down the line.
serviceDetail: A wet room installation in Stoneley typically begins with a proper survey of your existing bathroom. A qualified installer will assess the floor structure, existing drainage position, ceiling height, and the condition of walls before any design decisions are finalised. This stage matters more than many homeowners realise — skipping it is how projects run into trouble mid-way through. Once the survey is complete and a design agreed, the first physical stage is stripping the room back to the shell, removing existing sanitaryware, flooring, and wall coverings. The subfloor is then prepared and, if necessary, reinforced to take the weight of the new wet room base or screeded floor. A linear or central drain is set at the correct height to allow the floor to be graded towards it — typically a fall of around 1 in 80. Tanking comes next, which is the waterproof membrane applied across walls and floor to create a completely sealed wet zone. This is arguably the most critical part of the entire job and must be done with no gaps or weak points. Wall boards or tiles are then fixed over the tanking, shower valves and fittings are plumbed in, and any screens or glass panels are installed. The whole process for a standard Stoneley bathroom usually takes five to eight working days from strip-out to completion, though more complex projects in older stone-built properties may take longer.
pricing: Wet room installation in Stoneley typically ranges from around £6,000 to £12,000, depending on a number of factors. The size of the room is the obvious starting point, but the condition of the subfloor has a big impact — older stone properties sometimes need additional structural work before installation can begin. Choice of tiles, fittings, and screen type also moves the price significantly; entry-level materials sit at one end while premium porcelain tiling and designer fittings push costs toward the top of the range. Adding underfloor heating, which makes good sense in a wet room, adds roughly £500 to £900 to the project. Most Stoneley homeowners installing in a period property should budget toward the mid-to-upper end of this range to account for the unexpected.
whyLocal: Choosing a tradesperson who knows Stoneley makes a practical difference, not just a sentimental one. Local installers will have worked in the kinds of properties common to this part of Lancashire — they know what to expect when they lift the floor in a stone-built cottage or start chasing out walls in a Victorian terraced house. They're familiar with local building control requirements and the common quirks of Stoneley's housing stock. When something unexpected comes up mid-project (and it often does in older properties), a local professional can source materials quickly and keep the job moving rather than losing days waiting on deliveries.

faqs.q: Will a wet room work in an older stone-built property in Stoneley?
faqs.a: Yes, but it requires more thorough preparation than a modern home. Older properties in Stoneley often have solid or uneven floors that need levelling before waterproofing can begin. A good installer will survey the room first and flag any structural considerations. It's absolutely achievable — it just needs proper planning rather than rushing straight to installation.

faqs.q: How do I deal with limescale on my wet room fittings given Stoneley's water supply?
faqs.a: Stoneley is a moderately hard water area, so limescale on shower heads, screens, and chrome fittings is a real issue. Discussing a water softener or inline descaler during installation is worth it. Choosing matt or brushed finishes rather than polished chrome also helps, as limescale shows less and is easier to wipe away during routine cleaning.

faqs.q: How long will a wet room installation take in a typical Stoneley home?
faqs.a: Most standard wet room projects in Stoneley take five to eight working days from strip-out to final clean. Period cottages or stone-built homes with solid floors, limited access, or older plumbing connections may add a few extra days. Your installer should give you a realistic timeline after the survey — be cautious of anyone who quotes without seeing the room first.

faqs.q: Does a wet room add value to a Stoneley property?
faqs.a: Generally yes, particularly in mid-to-upper market homes. A well-finished wet room is seen as a premium feature and appeals strongly to buyers in Stoneley's market. The key is quality of finish — a poorly tiled or inadequately tanked wet room can put buyers off rather than attract them. Investing in proper installation protects both your enjoyment and resale value.
